Paragraph: Felled by a hail of arrows shot by Arjuna while standing behind Shikhandi, the grand sire Bhishma fell from his chariot, his body completely pierced such that it did not touch the earth, resting instead upon a bed of arrows. Surrounded by weeping warriors from both camps, Bhishma lay enduring excruciating physical torment, yet he retained complete mastery over his consciousness through his divine boon of Ichha-Mrityu (voluntary death). With his head hanging without support, he requested a pillow, rejecting soft cushions and accepting only three arrows from Arjuna to support his head. Refusing water from golden urns, he drank only the spring brought forth from the earth by Arjuna's arrow. As he lay suspended between life and death awaiting the auspicious Uttarayana, Bhishma endured boundless bodily agony while reflecting on his unyielding vows, his silent witnessing of past adharma, and his ultimate detachment from physical suffering.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Bhishma faces extreme physical torture and bodily destruction while suspended on a bed of arrows, coping with intense bodily pain alongside the psychological weight of his past systemic compromises while choosing to stay alive until the sacred solar movement.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Bhishma demonstrates supreme mental fortitude and sensory control, utilizing transcendental focus to master physical trauma, while accepting simple, rugged comfort (arrows for a pillow) over luxury.
Outcome/Resolution: He remains alive on the bed of arrows for weeks, transcending his physical agony to impart monumental discourses on ethics, governance, and liberation (Rajadharma and Mokshadharma) to Yudhishthira in the Shanti Parva.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Ichha-Mrityu (Voluntary mastery and control over the time and manner of one's death)
Shedha-Titiksha (Profound capacity to endure physical suffering and opposing dualities without complaint)
Deha-Adhyasa-Tyaga (Relinquishing attachment to the physical body and identifying with the eternal soul)
Sthitaprajna (Unshakable mental clarity and stability of mind in the midst of extreme physical adversity)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Bhishma's state on the bed of arrows illustrates 'Titiksha' (endurance) and freedom from 'Deha-Adhyasa' (body identification). By holding his life force through 'Ichha-Mrityu', he demonstrates that spiritual mastery allows an individual to remain anchored in higher consciousness (Sthitaprajna) even when the physical vessel is completely shattered.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This passage highlights extraordinary pain modulation, psychosomatic control, and dignity during end-of-life trauma. Bhishma relies on cognitive dissociation, extreme distress tolerance, and purpose-driven focus to override severe bodily agony, turning a traumatic death state into a period of profound wisdom transfer.
